2609.03663.title: Cross-Dataset Transfer and Reliability of Explainable Artificial Intelligence for RhythmFormer Remote Photoplethysmography
2609.03663.paper_summary: Background. Remote photoplethysmography estimates the cardiovascular pulse from facial video, and its explanations have rested on inspecting heatmaps rather than on quantitative evidence about where a model reads it. We quantified the explanations and asked whether such explanations transfer between datasets and track model performance. Method. We trained eight condition-specific RhythmFormer models on NCKU-rPPG, recorded under three illumination levels, speaking, rotation, and cycling, estimated one heart rate per 5.12-second clip, and set them beside a UBFC-rPPG reproduction. Raw attention, rollout, attention flow, and Beyond Intuition were assessed by skin coverage and the Salience-guided Faithfulness Coefficient (SaCo). Results. Beyond Intuition ranked highest on both datasets, at median coverage 0.789 and SaCo 0.837 on Static level 3 against 0.826 and 0.917 on UBFC-rPPG; lower ranks differed. Within one participant of one condition, neither measure was related to a clip's heart-rate error, waveform correlation, or signal-to-noise ratio on either dataset: 186 of the 252 coefficients fell below $|ρ|=0.10$ and 28 reached $p<0.05$ against the 13 expected by chance. Across the eight scenarios only Beyond Intuition's coverage followed the three performance measures, at $ρ=-0.43$, $+0.57$, and $+0.43$, while the attention-only methods' SaCo ran opposite to each. It failed at 40 lux alone, its median coverage falling to 0.180 and its median SaCo to $-0.178$, whereas motion degraded the estimates far more without such a drop. Conclusions. Skin coverage and SaCo carry information complementary to the performance measures rather than a proxy for them: attributing to the skin does not guarantee an accurate estimate. What an attribution reveals about a condition is where the model looks rather than how faithfully its map is ordered.
2609.03663.paper_summary_zh: 背景。遠程光電容積描記法從面部視頻估算心血管脈搏，其解釋依賴於檢查熱圖，而非關於模型讀取位置的定量證據。我們量化了這些解釋，並詢問這些解釋是否能在數據集之間轉移並追踪模型性能。方法。我們在NCKU-rPPG上訓練了八個特定條件的RhythmFormer模型，該模型在三個照明水平下錄製，包括說話、旋轉和騎自行車，估算每個5.12秒的片段一個心率，並將其與UBFC-rPPG的重現進行比較。通過皮膚覆蓋率和以顯著性引導的真實性係數（SaCo）評估原始注意力、回放、注意力流和超越直覺的表現。結果。超越直覺在兩個數據集上的排名最高，在靜態水平3的中位數覆蓋率為0.789，SaCo為0.837，而在UBFC-rPPG上分別為0.826和0.917；較低的排名有所不同。在一名參與者的單一條件下，無論是何種測量都與片段的心率誤差、波形相關性或信噪比無關：252個係數中有186個低於$|ρ|=0.10$，28個達到$p<0.05$，而預期的僅有13個。在八種情境中，只有超越直覺的覆蓋率跟隨了三個性能指標，分別為$ρ=-0.43$、$+0.57$和$+0.43$，而僅注意力方法的SaCo則與之相反。它在40 lux的情況下失敗，其中位數覆蓋率降至0.180，中位數SaCo降至$-0.178$，而運動則在沒有這種下降的情況下大幅降低了估算。結論。皮膚覆蓋率和SaCo攜帶的信息是對性能指標的補充，而非其代理：歸因於皮膚並不保證準確的估算。歸因所揭示的條件是模型的觀察位置，而非其地圖的秩序忠實度。
